title: The Research Process That Got Me 20 Viral Reels
summary: The creator shares her ideation and research process that has resulted in over 20 viral reels. The two-step process involves asking unhinged questions and diving into rabbit holes using voice dictation to capture ideas instantly.
key_points: Step 1: Questionmaxxing - Think of questions and be as unhinged as possible without judging yourself.
Step 2: The Rabbit Hole - Take an unhinged question from step one and dive deep into it.
Capture ideas the exact second they come into your head because walking through doorways or a few seconds of delay can make you forget them (the doorway effect).
Use a voice-to-text app like Wispr Flow to speak your thoughts instead of typing so you never lose the idea.
The creator claims she has dictated over 7 lakh (700,000) words using Wispr Flow, which equals nine Harry Potter books.
A question you have to type is a question you will decide is not worth asking, whereas a question you can just say gets asked.
content:
The RESEARCH process that got me 20 viral reels. I started making content seven months ago and since then more than 20 of my reels have crossed a million views. So the question I get the most is how are you thinking of your ideas? So you know what, I'll show you the ideation process. So let's start with step 1. It's called questionmaxxing. Your only job in this step is to think of questions and the only rule you need to remember is be as unhinged as you can. PAPA GOYAL. Is it genetic? Did I get it from my dad? Rajeev, [unclear]. STUCK. If I was stuck in an elevator and no one came to save me, would I die of hunger first or would I die of lack of oxygen first? WHO THOUGHT OF THIS? Who looked at a rock and thought if I move this up and down it will be good for my body? Was he just lazy? Did he just not want to farm? FARM WORK? NO THANKS. And once I have questionmaxxing, I go to step two, which is the rabbit hole. Basically take any one unhinged question from step one and dive into it. DON'T JUDGE. ChatGPT. IMPATIENCE? inherited. MY DAD. If impatience can be genetic, then my dad can just blame his dad. You know what? Find twin studies, if one person is [unclear] and one person is not, that means it's not genetic, it's upbringing. READING. Twin studies raised apart -> go deeper. Find me every separate twin study ever done. I wanna create a map of what I have inherited versus what's my upbringing. So if you notice during my entire research and ideation process, I have not typed once, and that's deliberate. ZERO KEYS PRESSED. The point is to catch the idea or in this case the question the moment it comes into your head because there's actual research that even a few seconds delay or you just walking through a doorway can make you forget that idea. It's literally called the doorway effect. WAIT... WHAT WAS IT? So what I do is use this app called Whisper Flow and I'm just speaking to it. By the way here are my Whisper Flow stats. Till date I have narrated 7 lakh words into this thing. 77,000 WORDS. And just so you know how much that is, the first Harry Potter book was 77,000 words. 9 BOOKS. So I have narrated the equivalent of nine Harry Potter books. This is what I'm doing in life, this is what I do on Friday nights, this is what I do on Saturday nights. WISPR x ME. So when Whisper Flow reached out for a collab, bro I would do it for free because I use you guys every moment of my day. ...I DIDN'T. But you know the sentiment is there. So I come bearing gifts. Wispr Flow PRO 3 months free. Only for the first 100 people. WAIT... What if two people click at the exact same second? Is it just whoever has faster Wi-Fi? Actually the people who are clicking are they just more impatient? Still questionmaxxing. Wispr Flow PRO 3 months free. 100 spots now open. First come, first served. How to claim yours: 1. Comment "curious rat". 2. I'll DM you the code. 3. Claim ASAP to secure your spot.
